claims.text: The as-homogenized HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a single-phase, solid-solution BCC alloy at room temperature.
Heating HfNbTaTiZr to approximately 400–1000°C reconfigures its dislocation structure.
Elevated temperature preferentially enhances edge-dislocation mobility in HfNbTaTiZr.
Temperature-induced dislocation changes reduce the elastic anisotropy of HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced elastic anisotropy moderates the thermal-expansion response relative to conventional BCC alloys.
Increased thermal energy activates edge-dislocation slip systems in HfNbTaTiZr.
Dislocation reconfiguration moderates the temperature-induced reduction of elastic moduli.
Anharmonic lattice vibrations coupled to an evolving dislocation network produce a distinct elevated-temperature deformation response.
Relative to room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr will show a smaller-than-expected decrease in elastic moduli.
The smaller-than-expected decrease in elastic moduli is caused by reduced elastic anisotropy.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a moderated, nonlinear thermal-expansion coefficient at elevated temperature.
The yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr will decrease as temperature increases.
The temperature-dependent decrease in yield strength is caused by activated dislocation motion.
The room-temperature elastic, yielding, and thermal-expansion responses are presumed to follow conventional BCC-alloy models.
The alloy remains single phase over the proposed approximately 400–1000°C test window.
Outside the specified temperature and single-phase limits, phase transformation or precipitation may dominate the response.
In-situ neutron diffraction can be used to determine temperature-dependent elastic anisotropy and elastic moduli.
